abstract_research_topics.justification: In-context learning deals with understanding the process in which models learn to adapt given a certain context, which is more theoretical.
This involves understanding how models behave when faced with data outside their expected context, a theoretical consideration.
This studies how models behave and can be improved when trained on data with noise, requiring theoretical insights.
Focuses on theoretical methods to leverage both labeled and unlabeled data in training.
Involves designing methods where the model generates its own supervision signals, a theoretical topic.
Studies how models can learn representations by contrasting positive and negative samples, fundamentally a theoretical approach.
A theoretical approach where models induce general rules from observed instances.
Involves integrating symbolic reasoning with neural networks, primarily theoretical.
Focuses on splitting and coordinating model training across systems, a theoretical challenge.
Similar to distributed deep learning, it handles the theories and methods of learning in distributed systems.
Explores the theoretical and methodical frameworks for training models across multiple systems or nodes.
Involves developing methods to ensure learning algorithms can operate at large-scale, a theoretical pursuit.
Similar to scalable machine learning but specifically for reinforcement learning, dealing with theory for large-scale RL applications.
Centers on theoretical models where algorithms actively query for data, a topic focusing on optimizing learning.
Studying how models can be updated and learn from data in a sequential manner, a classic theoretical subject.
Focuses on theoretical methods for adjusting learning rates to improve model convergence.
Also known as batch learning, concerning theoretical frameworks where models are trained on pre-collected datasets.

Widely used in diverse practical applications where models are trained with labeled data.
Concerns application of reinforcement learning techniques on static datasets, used in real-world scenarios.

Practical application where multiple agents learn to cooperate in dynamic environments.
Focuses on real-world situations where distributed agents or systems learn in a cooperative manner.
Application domain where multiple agents work together to optimize a common goal, found in real-world settings.
